key_insight: Representation Autoencoders (RAEs) can be scaled from ImageNet to open‑domain text-to-image generation by training large decoders on a frozen high-dimensional semantic encoder (SigLIP-2); scale improves general fidelity but performance also depends critically on targeted data composition.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between RAE-based diffusion modeling (successful on ImageNet) and large-scale, freeform text-to-image generation by providing a scalable, modular approach that leverages a frozen semantic encoder and large decoders.
method: Freeze a high-dimensional semantic encoder (SigLIP-2) to produce stable representation latents.
Train and scale RAE decoders (diffusion transformers) on a mixed corpus: web images, synthetic renders, and text‑rendered data to support freeform text conditioning.
Analyze how decoder scale and targeted dataset composition affect fidelity and generalization in text-conditioned generation.
impact: Enables modular, scalable T2I systems that reuse a fixed semantic encoder while improving fidelity via larger decoders and curated training data—reducing retraining costs and improving generalization for practitioners building large generative models.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: frozen SigLIP-2 encoder → latent space → scaled diffusion transformer decoder conditioned on text.
Dataset composition pie chart: proportions of web images, synthetic data, and text-rendered samples used for decoder training.
Scale vs. fidelity curve: decoder size on x-axis, image fidelity/generalization on y-axis, with annotations showing effects of data composition.
Before/after image grid: examples comparing small vs. large decoder outputs (same text prompts) to illustrate qualitative gains.
paper_title: Scaling Text-to-Image Diffusion Transformers with Representation Autoencoders
paper_authors: Shengbang Tong, Boyang Zheng, Ziteng Wang, Bingda Tang, Nanye Ma
